title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-22-maya
content:
Daily scratchpad - applied ML experiments
2026-03-22 (Maya Chen)

TL;DR:
- Ran quantized evals for rwd-open-13B variants (int4 static, q4f16, q8) on perf/testset-v2.
- Observed latency improvements ~2.8x with q4f16 but small quality drop on hallucination prompts.
- Next: run targeted prompt-sensitivity eval, create short regression set for canary.

TODO (today)
- [ ] Finish targeted hallucination prompts (10 examples) and add to regression set (by EOD).
- [ ] Re-run q4f16 with cache warm-up for >256-token contexts (Jordan to verify batching).
- [ ] Add eval logging to mlbench (save per-sample logits + perplexity).
- [ ] Draft short note for SRE about observed memory tail with q4f16 on p4d nodes.

Commands run (notes):
- ./mlbench/eval.py --model rwd-open-13B --quant q4f16 --data perf/testset-v2 --batch 4 --max-tokens 512 --out results/2026-03-22/q4f16.json
- ./mlbench/compare.py results/2026-03-22/{base.json,q4f16.json} --metrics ppl,edit-distance,answer-accuracy > results/2026-03-22/summary.txt

Quick results (head)
- baseline (fp16) : avg latency 520ms/token, ppl 12.4, accuracy@1 0.78
- q8              : avg latency 370ms/token, ppl 12.9, accuracy@1 0.76
- q4f16           : avg latency 185ms/token, ppl 13.8, accuracy@1 0.74
- int4-static     : avg latency 160ms/token, ppl 14.6, accuracy@1 0.69
Notes: latency numbers are per-token measured on p4d (full warm-up not guaranteed for some runs). q4f16 seems a good cost/latency sweet spot; int4-static gives bigger savings but more quality regression on QA-style prompts.

Prompt sets tried (high level)
- prompt-A (QA factual): 200 items from perf/testset-v2/qa-factual
- prompt-B (open-ended): 100 items from perf/testset-v2/open-ended
- prompt-C (hallucination stress): 50 adversarial prompts curated by Asha

Observed failure modes (examples)
- Hallucination prompt #12 (from prompt-C): q4f16 produced confident but incorrect citation compared to fp16 (fp16: "No source found", q4f16: "Study in 2019 by X found..."). Need targeted comparisons.
- Long-context cutoff: at ~3.2k tokens q4f16 logits got noisier; suspect KV cache quantization effects.

Notes for canary/regression set
- Create 40-example micro-regression set: 20 factual QA (sensitive to precision), 10 long-context coherence, 10 hallucination/adversarial. Keep short reference answers. Use for canary before deploy.

Instrumentation/metrics to capture
- per-sample ppl, token-level entropy, top-5 prob mass, hallucination flag (binary human label), latency p95, memory RSS, gpu-util.
- Persist per-sample outputs to S3 path: s3://rwd-experiments/2026-03-22/maya/q4f16/

Open questions / next experiments
- Is the hallucination increase due to weight quantization or kv-cache quantization? Plan: run a variant with fp16 KV cache + q4 weights (if supported) to isolate.
- How stable are q4f16 gains across different prompt distributions (chat-style vs docs)? Run one small chat-style sweep.
- Confirm cost model: estimate $/1000 tokens for each quant level using our cost calc (ask infra for updated p4d pricing).

Notes to SRE/Infra (short)
- Observed occasional OOM with int4-static when batch>6 on p4d. Not reproducible 100%. Attaching run ids in linked artifacts.

Meeting notes (quick)
- 1:1 with Jordan 2026-03-22: discuss canary rollout thresholds (target degrade <=2% accuracy, latency SLO p95 < 800ms per request for route test-chat).
- Sync with Asha 2026-03-22: finalize hallucination prompt list and start human-labeling.

Next steps (concrete)
- Create regression set + add to CI (small eval job, run on every model quantization PR).
- Run fp16-KV + q4 weights experiment (Ethan to spin up config).
- Draft internal note summarizing tradeoffs + recommendation for Dedicated tier canaries.

Scratch notes / miscellaneous
- If we keep q4f16 for Dedicated default, add explicit fallback to q8 for high-hallucination triggers.
- Consider storing short hashed prompt fingerprints to detect prompt drift in production.

End of scratchpad.
